clue.text: Game in which one's left standing

definitions.text: Game in which one's left standing

parts.words: Game in which one's left standing
parts.note: surface reading: a game whose winner is the last one still on their feet
setter's reading: when the music stops, the player without a seat is the one left on their feet, and is out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left standing' usually means surviving; in this party game being left standing means you have lost.
explanation.definitionFit: In this party game players circle seats while music plays, and whoever fails to grab a seat when it stops drops out.

clue.text: Join group of soldiers heading East

parts.note: a unit is a body of troops
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An enlistment: someone signs up with a regiment that is being sent eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' simply places the compass letter after the soldiers' word.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring things together into one, a plain synonym for the verb join.

clue.text: A number greeting almost pitifully?

indicators.note: something done pitifully is done badly, so the letters come out in a poor, jumbled order
almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a feeble, pitiful hello counts as a number.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the G from GREETING and rearrange GREETIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, positive, negative or zero, so it is one kind of number.

clue.text: Advertising first-rate circus

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
the ring is the arena of a circus, standing for the whole

explanation.surface: A billboard boasting about a top-class circus.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a classic mark of quality, originally from Lloyd's register of ships; crosswords often read the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing views or products means making them public, which is what advertising does.

clue.text: The way to power

parts.note: surface reading: the method by which someone becomes powerful
setter's reading: a literal passageway, from the phrase about the halls where government influence is wielded

explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase 'the corridors of power' means the places where political decisions are made, so a passage is literally the route there.
explanation.definitionFit: A long indoor passage is a way through a building, and the idiom ties such passages to governmental influence.

clue.text: A means of support, very large, incidentally

parts.note: taken as written
a prop holds something up
OS is short for outsize, the clothing label for very large

explanation.surface: An offhand remark about some huge scaffold or brace.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size abbreviation that crosswords use for very large.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word introduces a remark in passing, by the way, which is the adverbial sense of incidentally.

clue.text: One making a comeback?

parts.note: surface reading: a sportsman or performer returning after time away
setter's reading: a comeback is also a retort or reply, so this is someone who answers back

explanation.walkthrough: A comeback sounds like a return to form; here it is a quick reply, and the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who replies to a message or a challenge gives an answer, and a retort is one such answer.

clue.text: Design movement shows cunning in more ways than one

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the late Victorian decorative style led by William Morris

definitions.text: cunning in more ways than one
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... can both mean wiles or cunning, so the phrase holds two words for it

explanation.surface: A critic remarks that a decorative style is clever in several respects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In more ways than one' points to the two nouns in the phrase, each a synonym for trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement was named for its champions of handmade work, and both arts and crafts are old words for wily skill.

clue.text: Not doing enough work to get lead role in drama school

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two parts, studying too little

definitions.text: to get lead role in drama school
definitions.meaning: second meaning: learning a principal's part so as to step in, the way a stand-in actor trains

explanation.surface: A lazy drama student still hopes to land the starring part.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word after UNDER for the first sense; read whole, it is what a stand-in does to be ready to take over the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy prepares a leading actor's part to take over if needed, while splitting the word gives too little study.

clue.text: Terrorise drunken reveller

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk partygoer menaces those around him.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is a noisy, boisterous merrymaker, a close synonym for a reveller.

clue.text: Gum rinse specially prepared

indicators.note: something specially prepared has been made up afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist's mouthwash made up specially for sore gums.
explanation.walkthrough: Gum looks like the mouth's gums beside rinse; it is the sticky plant substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky secretion of trees, and gum is a closely related plant exudate, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Weapon put English in daze

indicators.note: put ... in tells us to place one piece inside the other

parts.note: to stun is to daze
Eng is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An order to use a weapon that leaves the English reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a lightweight British submachine gun, so it is a specific example of a firearm.

clue.text: Reform I am to establish

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
to prove something is to establish it as true

explanation.surface: A reformer declares an intention to set up something new.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I am' as the contraction I'm, then add a verb for establishing a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to make it better by change, which matches the verb meaning make better.

clue.text: Linen for New Year, perhaps, priest's wearing

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: the priest is something being worn, so his letter sits inside the other letters
perhaps suggests one possible arrangement, so the letters may be set out differently

parts.note: taken as written
P is a dictionary abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A priest dresses in fresh linen to celebrate New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' makes the priest the one inside: his letter goes into the year before the shuffle. Napery is a fairly rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is household linen, especially tablecloths and napkins, so linen is its plain meaning.

clue.text: Packed lunch?

parts.note: surface reading: food brought from home in a box
setter's reading: in Scotland a piece is a packed sandwich

explanation.walkthrough: In Scots a 'piece' is a sandwich taken to work or school; the answer really means bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word names a Scottish lunchbox sandwich meal, while the whole means done gradually in fragments.

clue.text: Unusual deposits from upper parts of ships

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of their ordinary order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strange encrustations scraped off the decks and upperworks of vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: The topsides of a ship are the parts of the hull above the waterline, its upper sections.

clue.text: Nocturnal prowler we'd encounter uprooted garden plant

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: pulling a plant up turns it upside down, which in a down entry reads it bottom to top

parts.note: a flower is a garden plant

explanation.surface: A horror tale: digging in the garden at night, we would meet a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a legendary man who turns into a wolf at full moon and roams by night.

clue.text: Casually macerate ingredients of meal

indicators.note: doing something casually means without care, so the letters are tossed into a careless order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A relaxed cook soaks the components of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon spread of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon repast of scones, clotted cream, jam and a pot of tea.

clue.text: Winding river possibly renamed

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements the letters might take

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A twisting river that has perhaps been given a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maeander in Turkey gave its name to every winding stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a loop or bend in a watercourse, named after a famously twisting Turkish waterway.

clue.text: Person arrested by a copper revealed in outline

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so this piece is held inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
the word cut short, as in pers. for person
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A suspect detained by a police officer is described in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief summary or quick insight, so a sketch or outline of something.

clue.text: Rustic form of fuel used around sanatorium

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: peat is cut and dried for burning
san is short for sanatorium

explanation.surface: A country sanatorium heated by a local fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: San is the old boarding-school word for the sick bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a country person, and a peasant is a poor farm worker of the countryside.

clue.text: Frenzied mother I can put at ease

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: put at ease suggests letters loosened up and allowed to settle in another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reassuring voice says it can calm a mother in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used as an adjective here, as in a maniac rage.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means wildly frantic or deranged, matching frenzied behaviour.

clue.text: State time (mean)

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a long period of time

explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a nation and time like a clock reading; both are verbs and nouns of another sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean of a set of numbers is what is usually called its average.

clue.text: Chief involved in some lawless behaviour

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: some and any are interchangeable determiners
arch means chief, as in archbishop or arch-rival

explanation.surface: A boss caught up in rowdy misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of disorder with no authority obeyed, essentially conduct without law.

clue.text: Look into firm's capital

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: An investor is told to examine a company's funds.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money beside firm's; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Egypt, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Quality of tyre rated poor

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters are in a damaged order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garage inspection marks a car tyre down as substandard.
explanation.definitionFit: The grooved rubber surface of a tyre is checked for depth, and its condition is a key measure of tyre safety.

clue.text: Rusting in taxi door finally eliminated, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way
the end of the word is removed, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A mechanic finds corrosion on a cab door and suspects it has finally been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but belongs to the fodder; DOOR loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen, so rusting is a particular chemical reaction of that kind.

clue.text: Explaining process involved in heating butter?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: gently melting butter to separate the milk solids, leaving it clear

explanation.surface: A cookery tutor explains what happens when you warm butter.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the act of making something understood and the kitchen technique that yields clarified butter.
